CORRECTION after reciprocal review. Original S4-B verdict (FAIL_WRONG_ENTITY, escalate_to_ceo) called this the Utah State Capitol based on a general neoclassical/columned gestalt match. The S4-A cross-review agent flagged a specific, checkable error before being cut off by an account usage limit: the column capitals in the photo are Ionic (paired spiral volutes), not Corinthian (acanthus leaves) -- and Ionic is specifically what the University of Utah's OWN Park Building has (built 1912, architects Dallas & Hedges, per multiple independent descriptions), whereas the Utah State Capitol is specifically documented as Corinthian (eight Corinthian columns on its pediment front, per SAH Archipedia / Utah History to Go). Independently re-verified by S4 (parent) directly: re-downloaded the disputed image and confirmed every visible column capital shows clear scroll/volute Ionic detailing, zero acanthus-leaf Corinthian ornamentation. This is strong, unambiguous evidence the photo is NOT the State Capitol and is consistent with a genuine University of Utah building (very likely Park Building, the campus's flagship Ionic-columned Neo-Classical building and a natural choice for the university's own homepage hero image), not a wrong-entity error. Reverting to PASS. Photo still lacks a recorded license (og:image scrape, no attribution available), so RIGHTS_REVIEW_REQUIRED stands unchanged from the original official-tier finding.
